purpose_of_this_fixture: Calibration fixture for the no-markers case (REAL-CALL-LESSONS C59; BUILD-PLAN 4.2 row s17). A discovery call with a wholesale plant nursery, exported by a meeting-assistant tool as a block export with a label-and-timestamp line above each paragraph. The file carries zero artifact markers: no square brackets, no ellipsis, no dash, no 'inaudible' or 'crosstalk' anywhere, every fragment under a confident full-name label. It is nonetheless heavily shredded (43 of 260 turns carry words owned by another speaker, and the three most load-bearing pain statements begin under our own label) and it holds one composite block: a 410-word paragraph under the sales manager's name that contains her own account, our question, the grower's answer with a vocative addressing the label, her reply, our recap and an assent nobody can own. The key asserts the repair: the absence of markers raises the doubt level instead of lowering it; grading is per turn, so the labelled speaker's clean turns elsewhere grade certain and Met while the block's segments are speaker-unresolved, cited side-only with the block range and capped at Partial until the user confirms who spoke; the decision-process criterion, whose detail lives only in the block, therefore grades Partial rather than Met (attributing the block to its label) or Missing (a file-level downgrade), and the verdict is Nearly ready instead of Discovery complete; talk share is refused because the block exceeds a few percent of the words; every fragment is re-joined to the turn carrying the semantic bulk, or held as 'boundary artifact, owner unresolved' where it could stand alone, and never re-attributed to a label. No reversal is guarded. Beside the intake assertions the 25 fields grade the call itself: three pains stated, two excavated, R4 met-with-residual, a Work Management build for availability, orders and despatch with quotes on the native CRM Deals/Opportunities board third in the client's own order.
transcript_format: Plain text block export, 779 lines: each turn is a header line 'Speaker Name MM:SS' followed by one text line, with a blank line between turns; 260 turns from 00:03 to 33:54, about 5,683 spoken words. Start-only timestamps, MM:SS, zero-padded, non-decreasing, no collisions and no inversions; no end times; no participant header and no call date. Four labels, all full names in one shape: 'Consultant', 'Teodora Okoro', 'Rasmus Wrenfield', 'Ilse Salvesen'. No bracketed cue, ellipsis, double hyphen or parenthesis appears anywhere, and no word such as inaudible or crosstalk; hesitation is rendered as ordinary words and commas. The export shreds sentences across labels in both directions: 33 turns begin with the closing word or words of the previous speaker's sentence (and a 34th, turn 104, may), and 10 turns end with the opening word of the next speaker's sentence, so 49 turns begin lowercase, 51 lack terminal punctuation and 44 are four words or fewer. Nothing in the export is bracketed, elided or flagged, and every fragment carries a confident full-name label, yet 43 turns hold words owned by another speaker and one block holds five speaker changes across six segments. Intake raises the doubt level from the shred and composite signals; a run that reads the absence of markers as cleanliness, or that skips the re-join pre-pass because nothing announced itself, fails this fixture.

The composite block (turn 183, 410 words under 'Teodora Okoro') is split into six candidate segments marked speaker-unresolved and nothing in it is attributed to the label. The decisive signal is the second-person address to the block's own label ('and Teodora you were in the room for this'); the interview move ('And who actually signs off on a change like this, if it's not you, is that Gunnar.') and the question-answer-acknowledgement chain corroborate it. Words against wall clock (410 words in 175 seconds) is inside the band and does not fire, so a detector relying on that signal alone misses the block.

Evidence from the block is cited side-only with the block range and capped at Partial until the user confirms the speakers. R7 is the proof: attribute the block to Teodora and it grades Met (wrong); discard the block and it grades Missing (wrong); side-only and it grades Partial (right), which is what makes the verdict Nearly ready rather than Discovery complete.

The cap is per turn, not per file. Teodora's clean turns (57, 62, 132, 172, 192, 232 among others) grade certain and Met; a file-level downgrade that punishes the whole transcript for one bad block, or distrusts every turn under her label, fails.

ai_opportunities.idea: A workflow that tells the grower on his phone when an order against a line he is growing is confirmed or cancelled, standing orders included, instead of a Friday printout.
An AI column that reads an emailed plant schedule into quote lines (species, size, quantity) so the sales manager prices from the board rather than retyping sixty lines.
An agent, limited to the client's workspaces, that flags a line promised on a live quote and sold on an order in the same week to the grower and the sales manager.
An AI column that drafts the credit reason from the driver's refusal note on the order line, for the office coordinator to confirm.
